text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it will cut its main interest rate to 35.76 percent annualy from 47.28 percent, from Monday.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet tentatively approved the this year's budget as part of preparations to launch a currency board system from July 1. Budget deficit is assumed at 6.2 percent of Gross Domestic Product in the draft.
-- Bulgaria's June monthly inflation is expected at six percent, slightly up from 5.6 percent in May, statistics experts said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to limit monthly wages of state firms' directors at up to 15 minimum wages in a move to curb budget spending. The minimum wage in Bulgaria is now set at 41,290 levs.
-- Japan may extend some $400 million to Bulgaria to upgrade the state coal-fired power plant Maritsa Iztok, Energy Committee chairman Georgi Stoilov said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet raised minimum pension to 27,000 levs from 16,300 levs.

-- Bulgaria is expected to tighten control on duty free shops at its borders in a move to crack down on illegal imports and curb annual losses of some $1 billion from unpaid customs duties, trade minister Valentin Vassilev said.
-- Amoco Corp. said it was selling its retail petrol stations in Bulgaria to Royal Dutch/Shell Group.

-- Head of the Open Society foundation George Soros arrived in Sofia to discuss economic developments in Bulgaria with senior government officials. President Petar Stoyanov is expected to award Soros with Bulgaria's top Stara Planina medal for his contribution to Bulgaria's post-communist development. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
